title.narrative: 2.2 GIS prosecutors and investigators equipped and deployed to various regional commands
- Equipment procured for prosecutors and investigators - Handover (event) of procured equipment

target.value: Procurement of office equipment (computers etc.) Handover of procured equipment to prosecutors and investigators

actual.value: 60 Computers procured for prosecutors and investigators, 3-year subscription to an online legal library (Digital Attorney). 10 computers procured for the intelligence department 8 computers for the Policy Planning Monitoring and Evaluation Department (PPMED) Equipment handed over to the GIS by the Danish Deputy Ambassador on 24 July 2024 (annex 3_Final acceptance certificate and Handover note, annex 4_Media coverage of handover ceremony)

title.narrative: 3.1 Capacity of GIS management on strategic planning, result based budgeting and action planning is strengthened
- # of trainings for GIS management conducted - # of border management conferences held - # of consultation meetings with GIS management (HQ and regional commanders) held

target.value: Training of GIS management/heads of departments, sections, sectors and units on strategic planning, results based budgeting and developing action plans Consultation meeting with GIS management ((HQ and regional commanders) Border management conference to foster inter-agency experience sharing and exchange with other government agencies

actual.value: GIS management and Regional Commanders were trained on Results Based Management and Strategic Planning in from 17-21 October 2022. The workshop also presented an opportunity to brainstorm with GIS management on the vision, mission and direction for the new GIS Strategic Plan The project facilitated the participation of representatives from the GIS and Customs to two International Border Management conferences held in Amman Jordan (November 2022) and Istanbul, Turkiye (December 2023), where they both participated in panel discussions and shared their experience with their counterparts from several other countries. In 2023, the project collaborated with the SBS project, funded by the EUTF and implemented by ICMPD to organise a sub-regional border management workshop that brought together border officials from Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire, Togo and Burkina Faso for a 2-day workshop on 15-16 November 2023.

title.narrative: 2.1 GIS prosecutors and investigators trained to investigate and prosecute migration related offences
- Validated gaps and needs assessment of the GIS legal department - # of prosecutors trained - # of investigators trained as trainers

target.value: 1. At least 30 Prosecutors trained and certified. 2. At least 20 Investigators trained as trainers.

actual.value: 1. Gaps and needs assessment of the GIS Legal Directorate conducted and report validated on 23 June 2022. 2. 30 prosecutors trained and certified following a 6-week course from 20 June – 29 July 2023. 3. 25 GIS officers trained on the fundamentals of Intelligence gathering, 04 – 08 July, and analysis, 19 – 24 September 2022.

target.value: Gaps and needs assessment of the GIS legal department to define the training and equipment needs At least 30 Prosecutors trained and certified At least 20 Investigators trained as trainers

actual.value: Gaps and needs assessment of the GIS legal department conducted and assessment report validated on 23 June 2022 30 GIS investigators were trained in two sessions of training: 10-day basic training from 7-18 August 2023, 4 weeks advanced training from 22 Jan-16 Feb. 2024. 10 investigators trained as trainers from 17-21 June 2024 (annex 2_ToT report) 30 GIS officers trained and certified as prosecutors from 20 June -29 July 2022

target.value: Gaps and needs assessment of the GIS legal department to define the training and equipment needs.

title.narrative: 1.2 A functional fraud office established and commissioned in Kumasi to cover the Ashanti, Bono, Brong Ahafo, Western and Northern regions
- Fraud office space renovated and equipped - # of sensitization activities conducted

target.value: Assessment of GIS Ashanti regional command to determine needs and gaps Renovation of fraud office space Procurement of forensic and office equipment

actual.value: Gaps and needs assessment of Ashanti regional command conducted and assessment report validated on 22 June 2022 Fraud office renovated and commissioned on 24 August 2023. Forensic and office equipment procured and installed in the fraud office. Extensive media coverage of the commissioning event contributed to the sensitisation drive. Flyers (500 copies) on the services provided by the office were produced and distributed widely across Ashanti, Ahafo, Bono and Bono East Regions.

target.value: Assessment of GIS Ashanti regional command to determine needs and gaps.

title.narrative: 1.1 Capacity of GIS officers in the select regions strengthened in detection and investigation of document fraud cases

- Validated report on the gaps and needs of the Ashanti regional command towards the establishment of a fraud office
- # of officers trained on document fraud detection in at least three select regions (Ashanti, Ahafo and Bono regions)
- # of officers trained on intelligence gathering and investigation
- Doc 2 certified officers deployed to regional offices
- SOP developed for the fraud office

target.value: 100 officers trained on document fraud detection 50 officers trained on intelligence gathering and investigation Doc 2 certified officers deployed to regional offices SOP for new fraud office developed

actual.value: 100 officers trained on document fraud detection across Ashanti, Ahafo, Bono and Bono East regions (25 trained per region) between October and November 2023. 55 officers trained (30 on intelligence gathering and analysis, 25 on investigations)2 Doc2 officers have been deployed to the Kumasi office in July 2023. SOPs developed for the Fraud office in May 2024 and embedded in the SOP of the Ashanti command.(merged with Result 3.2)

title.narrative: 1. Strengthen the capacity of GIS staff to detect forged and falsified travel documents, impostors and identity theft

Outcome indicator I - Increased capacity of GIS to detect forged or falsified document and improved profiling -Improved capacity to prosecute document fraud and other migration related offences, to secure convictions. -Increased intra-agency cooperation on investigation and prosecution of offences

target.value: Improved capacity at the regional level to detect, investigate and prosecute document fraud and other migration related offences.

actual.value: Capacity of GIS to detect document fraud has improved with the renovation and operationalisation of the Document Fraud Office in Kumasi; training of officers on document fraud detection; and training of prosecutors, investigators and intelligence officers.

title.narrative: 2. Strengthen the capacity of GIS staff to investigate and prosecute migration related cases.
- Improved capacity to prosecute document fraud and other migration related offences, to secure convictions. - Increased intra-agency cooperation on investigation and prosecution of offences.

target.value: GIS officers trained to investigate and prosecute migration related cases

actual.value: Capacity of GIS to investigate and prosecute have improved with the training of 30 prosecutors; training of 30 investigators and exchange session/training of the legal directorate by the judicial service.

title.narrative: 4.4 Increase GIS resistance to cyber threats through improved professional capacities of Cybersecurity unit staff
- Assessment of training needs - Training curricula and manuals developed - At least 100 GIS officers trained on Cybersecurity at basis, intermediate and advanced levels

target.value: Assessment conducted At least 100 officers trained on cybersecurity Cybersecurity training manual and curricula developed At least 20 staff members of cybersecurity unit trained and certified at professional level At least 2 officers go on internship abroad

actual.value: Assessment conducted and report validated 130 officers (30 in 2023 and 100 in July 2024)trained on cybersecurity at the foundation level (annex 9_cybersecurity awareness report) 2 manuals on cybersecurity developed: Entry level and Post entry training manuals (annex 10 and 11) 20 Officers went through the international certification at the foundation level in August 2023. 25 officers trained and certificated at the intermediate/advanced level (annex 12) 10 officers participated in a study visit to Czech Republic (annex 13)

title.narrative: 4.1 Cybersecurity Unit’ and Committee’s role and place within GIS approved
Cybersecurity committee and unit operational.

target.value: Concept of Cybersecurity unit and Cybersecurity Committee well engineered Roadmap for unit implementation approved Appropriate HR resources allocated Job profiles designed

actual.value: Assessment of GIS Management Information System Department (MISD) and recommendations for the set-up of a cybersecurity unit (including job profiles and structure of the unit) concluded and validated on 12 April 2023

title.narrative: 2.3 GIS legal department exchange and share experience with their counterparts in other GoG agencies (Attorney General’s office, Ghana Police etc.)

- # conference between prosecutors from GIS, GPS, Attorney general’s office etc. to share experience and strengthen collaboration. - # conference between investigators from GIS, GPS, NIB, EOCO etc. to share experience and strengthen collaboration.

target.value: Two annual conference on strengthening interagency cooperation for the prosecution of offenders #Two annual conferences on strengthening interagency cooperation for the investigation of offenders

actual.value: From 23-24 May 2023, an exchange session/training was organised between the GIS legal directorate and two justices from the high courts. The training of 30 investigators (2.1.3) was done in collaboration with the Ghana Police Service, Economic and organised Crime Office and the judicial services. This allowed for experience sharing and strengthening of inter-agency collaboration. Consultation meetings on the review of the GIS law (Act 573) was organised between the Law Review Committee and GIS regional commanders (21-22 May 24) and other government agencies, academia and private sector (27-28 May 2024) to discuss proposed amendments to the law, aimed at strengthening GIS operations, proposing stiffer penalties for offences and facilitating movement. In addition, a technical meeting with the Ministry of Justice and Attorney General Department took place from 09-11 July 2024 to discuss the proposed amendments to the GIS Law (annex 5_report of consultation meetings)

title.narrative: 3.2 The new GIS 2023 – 2027 Strategic Plan is drafted, validated and launch by the Government of Ghana

- Strategic Plan Technical Working Group (SP-TWG) inaugurated - First draft strategic plan (SP) developed - Accompanying SP action plan developed - SP M&E framework developed - SP tentative budget developed - Strategic plan, action plan and M&E framework finalised and validated - Adoption and Launch of the GIS 2023 – 2027 SP - GIS regional commands sensitized on new SP

target.value: SP-TWG inaugurated SP Action plan, budget and M&E framework finalised and validated Launch of GIS 2023-2027 SP Sensitisation of regional commands on new strategic plan

actual.value: SP-TWG inaugurated on 13 October 2022 First draft of SP developed on during a drafting session from 13-15 December 2022 The SP, action plan and M&E framework were finalised and validated between 12 and 14 July 2023 SP budget developed following a budgeting session from 28-30 March 2023 The SP was officially launched by the Minister of the Interior on 11 October 2023 SP Action plan, budget and M&E framework finalised and validated 300 officers selected across all GIS regional, sector, district and municipal commands sensitised on the new strategic plan and action plan between 24 June-05 July 2024
